subject: Refractive index
hook: REFRACTIVE INDEX IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK
angle: Refractive index can be less than 1—water’s index for 30 keV X‑rays is 0.99999974, slightly below vacuum
angle_support: This can occur close to resonance frequencies, for absorbing media, in plasmas, and for X-rays. In the X‑ray regime the refractive indices are lower than but very close to 1 (exceptions close to some resonance frequencies).
As an example, water has a refractive index of 0.99999974 = 1 − 2.6×10⁻⁷ for X‑ray radiation at a photon energy of 30 keV (0.04 nm wavelength).
title: Why Water Is Faster Than Light
description: We explore how the refractive index of water can fall below one when interacting with X-rays. This phenomenon challenges the common assumption that light must always slow down in matter.
narration: REFRACTIVE INDEX IS NOT WHAT YOU THINK You picture a number that must always be higher than one. It was closer to the idea that light always slows down when entering a dense material. Actually, the refractive index can drop below unity. For X-rays at 30 keV, water exhibits an index of 0.99999974. This occurs because the phase velocity of these high-energy waves briefly exceeds the speed of light in vacuum. The laws of physics allow light to behave in unexpected ways.
